text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses training data—examples that include both inputs and correct answers—to build a model. This model is essentially a set of rules or patterns that the computer discovers from the data. After training, the model can make predictions on new, unseen information. For instance, it might predict house prices based on size and location. To improve reliability, we measure the model’s accuracy, which tells us how often its predictions match the real outcomes. The more quality training data we have, the better the model becomes.
